title_en: PSA: Doomscrolling in GTA 6 Is a Necessity if You Want To See Everything the World Has To Offer
summary_en: Scrolling social media in GTA 6 is more than a distraction - it can help you see everything the world has to offer.
body_en:
Ever since that first trailer , we knew social media would play an important part in GTA 6. A good chunk of those first 90 seconds was faux TikTok footage, after all. And now that reviews are out , and the game is live in New Zealand, Australia, and many other places on that side of the planet, we have a better idea of how GTA 6’s in-universe social media operates. One thing’s for certain: you’ll need to be scrolling if you want to see everything the world has to offer.
As part of IGN’s Ask Me Anything livestream earlier today, reviewer Luke Reilly explained how he unlocked a new mission chain based on a post he saw on Snapmatic, the GTA universe’s parody of Instagram.
“I was scrolling through the game’s social media, and I saw a post from this guy on a farm looking for a pilot, and it pings it on the map for you,” he said. “It’ll ping in an undiscovered part of the map that there’s something there because you’ve spotted it on social media.”
IGN’s Simon Cardy, who has also played over 100 hours of the game and is currently answering your questions over on our launch live blog , confirms that he also used social media to discover new opportunities, which are then automatically pinned to the game’s map.
Simon also notes that you’ll hear about opportunities on the in-game radio, although those are hints you’ll need to follow up on yourself – only certain mediums will pin a mission to your map. Aside from social media posts, pamphlets on local bulletin boards will also drop mission markers on your map, something Luke described in today’s AMA: “One of the cool things is that you see signs around [advertising] for a pilot. It’s visual storytelling; you can [follow the instructions] and go there and do jobs for this character that you meet.”
Bulletin boards are, of course, nothing new for video games – you’ll no doubt have picked up hundreds of bounties and side quests from boards in dozens of RPGs across the years. But GTA 6’s use of the internet and social media is more novel. Simon also notes that there are connections to be found across the in-game web, too – a story on the news app may lead you to investigate a topic on Snapmatic, which in turn will pin a new mission to the map.
In short: we may call it doomscrolling in real life, but it’s a pretty handy activity to do in GTA 6. While I expect there will be multiple ways to stumble across the game’s many, many missions, it seems a fun and authentic method to discover things on social media.
For more GTA 6, be sure to check out our breakdown of how long it takes to complete its campaign , as well as our brand new interview with Rockstar’s Rob Nelson . And if you want to see the game in action, you can watch 15 minutes of the game’s first mission .
Matt Purslow is IGN's Executive Editor of Features.
